value.rationale: The relation between first-hit species richness and second-hit richness is a natural joint occupancy-dependence observable; its sign switches from competition at low load to common near-saturation behavior at high load. The result provides the complete all-sample-size one-switch classification for every fixed uniform box count and a universal asymptotic loading threshold, not a chosen numeric example, table entry, or routine rephrasing of an exact moment formula. It marks when first and second discovery counts cease to be negatively correlated and can guide interpretation of joint occupancy fluctuations.
